description.value: The study investigated cognitive and cortical structural differences associated with low versus high recent levamisole exposure among chronic cocaine users, compared with stimulant-naive controls.

spans.text: The aim of the present studies was to examine whether the worldwide highly prevalent cocaine adulterant levamisole is associated with higher risks for cognitive impairment and structural brain alterations in chronic CU with recent levamisole exposure.

value: we hypothesized that higher levamisole exposure is associated with more severe cognitive dysfunctions.
we expected that high levamisole exposure is linked to cortical thinning explicitly in the frontal lobe.

description.value: Cross-sectional case-control studies comparing chronic cocaine users with low or high recent levamisole exposure and stimulant-naive controls; Study 2 used structural MRI.

structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
All subjects were scanned using a 3T Philips Achieva whole-body scanner equipped with a 32-channel receive head coil.

High-resolution structural scans were collected using a standard T1-weighted 3D magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) pulse sequence with repetition time (TR) = 8.08 ms, echo time (TE) = 3.7, field of view (FOV) = 240×240 mm, 160 slices, voxel size of (1×1×1)mm .
